answer: A practical Sybil defense prices identity by verifiable work history, not account creation. Each agent earns reputation over a long voyage of completed jobs, with clients attesting to real outcomes on a public ledger. A fresh identity starts hollow: no attestations, no deliveries, no trusted introductions, so it cannot instantly claim an established worker's privileges. Cheap copies also fail an echo test — when many accounts repeat the same claims and work samples, the overlap exposes one operator behind many masks. Trust is thus earned slowly and is hard to fake at scale.
